7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1 There is a documented policy and procedure for Neonatal services.

7.2 The policy for care of neonatal patients is in consonance with the national/ international guidelines.

7.3 Those that care for children have age specific competency.

7.4 Provisions as permitted by state law are made for special care of neonates.

7.5 Patient assessment includes detailed nutritional, growth, and immunization assessment.

7.6 Documented policies and procedures prevent neonate abduction and abuse.

7.7 The children’s family members are educated about nutrition, immunization and safe parenting and this is documented in the medical record.

8. 0 PROCESSES

• SOP of Newborn Care Corner (NBCC)

Background:

A neonatal Care Corner is a space within a delivery room in a health facility where immediate care is provided to all newborns at birth.

Expected Services to be provided at the NBCC

Newborn Care Corner

Care at birth

• Prevention of infection

• Provision of warmth

• Resuscitation

• Early initiation of breastfeeding

• Weighing the newborn

Care of Normal Newborn

• Breastfeeding/feeding support

Care of sick newborn

• Providing Phototherapy for newborns with Hyper-bilirubinemia

• Identification and prompt referral of 'at risk' and 'sick' newborn Setup; A separate area of 20-30ft in size within the labor room with all facilities for establishing newborn corners.

• Requirements:

a) Manpower:

A. Pediatrician – 1

B. Resident – 1

C. Technician – 1

D. Nursing staff – 1

b) Materials:

1. Phototherapy Unit

2. Resuscitation trolley with necessary equipment’s

3. Oxygen cylinder, hood, Nasal Prongs, Mask ,

4. Neonatal suction machine

5. Infusion pump

6. CIPAP machine

7. Emergency drugs with different IVF

8. Nebulizer

9. Phlegm suction machine

10. Miscellaneous

Procedure: First vitals are checked to assess the diagnosis. If vitals are not established then resuscitation is provided to the neonate with the help of equipments& medications. As per condition of the baby necessary management is provided in NBCC.

Precautions: Regular aseptic precautions, fumigation, change of draw sheets are mandatory. If the baby is in a very critical condition then after giving first aid, the neonate is referred in an ambulance to a higher centre for further management & care.

Scientific observations: There is proven efficacy due to timely NBCC care in all critical conditions in comparison with routine care to reduce infant mortality rate.

Facility Based Newborn Training Program- All the personnel involved in NBCC management have undergone hands on training in BNCRP (Basic newborn care & Resuscitation Program-1)

8.2 Hospitals follow national and international guidelines available for the case of neonates by WHO. The hospital is actively promoting breast feeding practice.(Ref. Newborn Care Corner (NBCC) Protocol Policy)

8.3 The Newborn Care Corner (NBCC) is fully equipped and the Nurse- patient ratio is 1:1. Those who care for children have age specific competency and training.

8.4 Adequate amenities for the care of neonates to be available in the hospital, for example, a breast-feeding room.

8.5 Nutritional, growth, and immunization assessment: To be documented and it should be maintained using a standard format.

8.6 The organization ensures that there is adequate security/surveillance to prevent neonate abduction and abuse. There are security cameras and tags for identifications.

8.7 The children’s family members are educated about growth charts, immunization charts, etc. This (original/copy) should be a part of the medical record. The education is preferably be in the regional language that the family understands
